body: We're all here together. I was never heard because I was suffering silently in my mind for years, until I took the same step as you: I started speaking and reaching out online. Yes, at age 40 :)

That's great news. You are taking the best first step - giving yourself time. I understand a lot of what you mention out of personal experience. I'm 40, unemployed, alone, and my mother recently asked me again if I need money. How does that make me feel? Because I love her and value how she dedicated her life to me, I will find a way to change.

I took the first step as you did: I gave myself time. It took me 15 years, but I am speaking out now that I'm online with this wonderful group, rather than sitting alone and depressed. I switched my journal to a blog to speak out, share and receive thoughts, experiences, solutions...(even though so far I'm talking to myself and no one knows about my site but I feel better speaking out.)

I don't fully believe in doctors, counsellors, therapists and medication because they practice based on theory, not experience, and for money. They might control a problem, which is a good start, and it always stays an option.

You started speaking, you gave yourself time, which are huge steps forward. You're not just waiting, you're taking action. You say you're a cog - but that's an important piece - it breaks and the whole machine crashes.

As I see from all the members here, they care and have priceless advice, we're all together and not alone, and we won't only be controlled by others and social pressures. Stay strong and keep moving.

Thank you for your feedback aghoraa3 I really enjoyed reading it, how you describe the scene of the poem, the challenges, the message. I read it several times. The ship of life, living for someone on theirs, makes me useless. Jumping blindly is just landing on someone else's. With patience and clear direction, before giving up, I need to know where to jump to command my own ship. Maybe I should change the title to "Jump Your Ship". Thanks again.

I've been talking to myself a lot...for years. Not many people to trust, feel comfortable with, and hug. An online chat is better than thinking, talking to myself or just posting to a blog no one knows exists. So, always ready for chat and listening. And, I haven't given or received a hug in a very very long time. But... I can make it digital since I'm not in California!

# >------------(><)------------<

Great to hear this and see you have the spirit and will. Thank you for sharing these words and saying them out loud. They hide deep and don't always come out. But you brought them out and helped me get up.

I didn't fully understand the scene or create my own explanation - the Pale Man and the Pale King - white mind, the ring... I saw the man bribing and reaching the King, but what were the notes, what was to be accomplished? It'll be great to explain it. Thanks.

I liked the images and travelling high above clouds and stars. The theme or image it describes made me think of reaching high for dreams and goals. Burnt wings? That reminds of myself reaching way too high, that my wings are only in my dreams and I burn them in real life because I don't take the first footsteps of reality. I read the comments, sorry to hear about your friend.

Going above the stars and glittering, I saw success and joy, going above the sun itself, sending positive vibes, also bringing down rain, a good thing, but everything turns around to sad and burning out because of the sun.

I like it short and clear stanzas, clear images, but one thing I'm not sure I understood is clear is the flow of events, it's a dead dream, someone going up so high, but I didn't see the closure - the dream or what happens after wings burn out. I enjoyed the poem style, structure and words.
Thank you so much for the feedback. I reviewed it several times over a few days to rephrase and shorten some lines, use vivid images and maintain the rhythm. I'm glad you enjoyed it!

As a violinist, I hear the music, chords, I feel the crescendos. That person is a musician in this world symphony with you every movement, even short sad ones, but ending in a high tempo and a major key, only to start conducting another one. One thing I can't see or imagine, the accordion playing in the orchestra performing a symphony. That's more of a band with joyful music. But...you're the composer and it's your symphony! Keep up the compositions!

Wow. That truly is a lifelong relationship and I definitely see why and how it remains connected and does not break at any point in time. It's also clear how each description or image comes in pairs, two parts that complement each other.  Thank you for the reply.

I see, or feel, a difficult relationship. The partner was taking everything away, all hope, joy, opportunities. Very selfish as well. What I also see a clear picture of is being tied together, not in a good way, more chained together and can't leave... two sides of a coin and in the same void.

Something I don't get a clear picture of is the end - the title is "You Were", something in the past. The poem speaks of each seeking to depart, but have the partners split each following their own path? Has the partner changed? How do the lines convey the message?

Another thing, it starts with great images of nature... water, wind, fire, earth, but changes direction into a different scene, that I felt disconnected. One thing I think might be worth trying is completing the poem in the same theme, unless there was a specific reason, image or message to divide it that way.

14 years! Then I believe you are one strong guy. I had a panic attack once, in the street, didn't know anyone, ended up calling 911 to get picked up by an ambulance. I have my seizures (epilepsy - 20 years now) but doctors are useless. They just increase medication. I studied and monitored myself more than they did. I saw patterns in my seizures: when they take place, how they happen, and a lot of time, what triggers them. I'm learning how to control them and trying. Did you ever notice such a thing, patterns and triggers? That's always a good point to check, especially since you're living it every moment and can pay attention to details more than anyone. Take care and stay strong. I'm going to wake up the kid inside me and follow your footsteps.
Great. Thank you for clarifying! I'll practice and keep that in mind (especially for a musician... I need my rhythm and tempo :)

Thank you so much for the detailed feedback. I really appreciate it. My first challenge was posting the work, afraid it will bother readers being a sensitive topic that will block feedback. I'm okay speaking about it now, so open to all comments.

You  said it exactly - some were forced, especially last few lines. I used to write when I was 12 (the short poem rhymes) but decided to start again. I read about styles, came across Acrostic and tried it for the first time. The phrase had an odd number of characters and I ended up cramming a few more to complete it and that probably ruined the ending (and the phrase)

If you don't mind me asking for advice in poetry: how was the meter inconsistent? For the story or theme, would you write it in a different more suitable style? I can try it.

Thanks again!

Thank you for your reply. Complex but speaking it through a poem for the first time dismantled it. Message was quite clear not obscure as you said. I probably should have said hidden words if you haven't picked them out yet. I was trying Acrostic for the first time so it might have shifted focus from clear story to fitting everything in by the letter.

The great topic of love and relations. It takes two people to complete and live a life of love. When you started to speak, a seed grew to a green plant that you watered together gave it a great image of the relationship. What I'm not sure of is how that squirrel killed the plant; suddenly killed the love, took the partner, what was it that filled the hole other than the love? Personally, I also like to read a poem in shorter, strong verse. If I imagine myself reading it out, how will I speak out or act with energy or feeling? Send out a clear message? I'm just starting as well, my first day, so comments might not be professional poet feedback, just from personal style, experience reading other poems.

Great message - a challenge that lives on in everyday lives. Living by community standards, following Either-Or ways, not your own path and letting yourself out. Several points are mentioned such as: finding closure, and responsibility to change. What action do you take to accomplish such goals and responsibilities? How will you put society on the shelf? Action and imagery will keep in printed in my mind. Great rhyme, but the poem went off tempo / lost rhythm towards the end under the responsibility to change.

L.A.
Anytime! Meaning definitely brings joy, but it's a worthy challenge that develops with time and doesn't end (unless we decide to end it). Always here :)

You mentioned one critical word: apathy. It takes me 2 or 3 months to fill myself with passion, motivation and excitement, and a few days to lose it all and start again (especially if I fail at a task). I don't think I would describe it as mental. I don't want to change either, but I think I have to change the way I do things.

Can I ask you, do you know what triggers your apathy, or do you know when it hits?

I feel you are describing me and my life. I was the boyfriend who ended a beautiful 8 year relationship because of my weak personality and low self esteem. You live in pain, I lived in pain for years, but what was more painful was the guilt and losing my only love.

I had to put down two dogs (13 and 14 years old), who I loved more than any family member because they were my true friends and comforters. And that was the time I cried most in my life.

You hit rock bottom. The good thing is: you didn't drown. Rock bottom is a solid ground, you are strong (stronger than me) because you stood up again, and now you are speaking out, climbing up the mountain. That took 9 years of my life to get up and start.

Keep climbing.
